'''Rajesh Shukla''' (born 1 August 1965) is an Indian researcher, author and applied statistician.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/author/rajesh-shukla|title=Shukla, Rajesh|date=5 February 2019|website=SAGE Publications Inc|language=en-us|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> His major area of work is the Indian Consumer landscape and citizens’ environment. Shukla has served as the Director for [[National Council of Applied Economic Research|NCAER]]-Centre for Macro Consumer Research<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-business/NCAER-sets-up-centre-for-consumer-research/article16003448.ece|title=NCAER sets up centre for consumer research|date=18 March 2010|work=The Hindu|access-date=2019-02-05|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/north/knowledge-hub-of-india-is-ncr-dr-rajesh-shukla-former-director-ncaer-cmcr/articleshow/12835776.cms|title='Knowledge hub of India is NCR: Dr Rajesh Shukla, Former Director, NCAER-CMCR|last=Alang|first=Astha|date=23 April 2012|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> and is a visiting professor at Institute for Human Development (IHD), India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.orfonline.org/research/how-do-you-measure-new-movements/|title=How do you measure new movements?|website=ORF|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ihdindia.org/Rajesh-Shukla.html|title=Institute for Human Development|website=www.ihdindia.org|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> He is currently serving as the Managing Director & CEO of People Research on India's consumer economy (PRICE, branded as ICE 360<sup>0</sup>), an independent not-for-profit ‘think-tank’ cum ‘fact-tank’, engaged in identifying data gaps, collecting, building and disseminating seminal knowledge and insights into India's Citizens’ Environment and Consumer Economy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ice360.in/|title=Home – People Research on India's Consumer Economy|website=ice360.in|access-date=2019-02-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ibef.org/news/99-indian-households-are-covered-by-a-bank-account|title=99% Indian households are covered by a bank account|website=www.ibef.org|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.floroscent.com/wgc-tracks-global-gold-market-next-30-years/|title=WGC tracks the global gold market over next 30 years|date=25 May 2018|website=Floroscent|language=en-US|access-date=2019-01-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ice360.in/en/projects/about-us/team|title=Team – People Research on India's Consumer Economy|website=www.ice360.in|access-date=2019-02-14}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
He received his MSc (1989) and PhD (1993) in Agricultural Statistics from [[Indian Agricultural Research Institute|Indian Agriculture Statistics Research Institute (IASRI)]], India and BSc (1985) in Agriculture from [[Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology|N.D. University of Agriculture & Technology (NDUAT)]], India.

In 1993, he has started his career as survey statistician at [[National Council of Applied Economic Research]] (NCAER), the India's oldest and largest independent economic think tank, reached highest level in research ladder as the Senior Fellow (NCAER) in 2004 and became the Director of NCAER-CMCR.

Shukla has created Pan India primary baseline databases on issues of national importance, analytic constructs, and actionable insights relating to household well-being;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/opinion/measuring-household-well-being/245128/|title=Measuring household well-being|date=29 April 2016|website=The Financial Express|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> income distribution and inequality;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/addressing-income-distribution/737557/|title=Addressing income distribution|date=15 January 2011|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> regional disparity;<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/opinion/et-commentary/inclusive-growth-regional-disparity/articleshow/5408319.cms|title=Inclusive growth & regional disparity|last=Shukla|first=Rajesh|date=4 January 2010|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> Rural & Urban well-being;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/opinion/rural-urban-continuum-and-the-lessons-for-india/117761/|title=Rural-urban continuum and the lessons for India|date=12 August 2015|website=The Financial Express|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> Financial Inclusion;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Opinion/cltWOaGU1h8JsUgidVx6mL/Financial-inclusion-20.html|title=Financial inclusion 2.0|last=Rajadhyaksha|first=Cafe Economics {{!}} Niranjan|date=7 December 2010|website=Mint|language=en|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref>  Indian Middle Class,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/india-s-middle-class-population-to-touch-267-mn-in-5-yrs-111020600069_1.html|title=India's middle class population to touch 267 mn in 5 yrs|agency=Press Trust of India|date=6 February 2011|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2019-02-05}}</ref> Tourism;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Shukla |first=Rajesh |date=2006 |title=Tourism Satellite Account for India |url=https://ideas.repec.org/p/eab/develo/22176.html |journal=Development Economics Working Papers |language=en |publisher=[[East Asian Bureau of Economic Research]] |article-number=22176}}</ref> Science and Technology;<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://philpapers.org/rec/BAUTCO-2|title=The Culture of Science: How the Public Relates to Science Across the
